headline: Mistakes to Avoid When Hooking Up New Kitchen Appliances
articleBody:
Installing new kitchen appliances should be an exciting milestone, but small coordination oversights can lead to costly rework, water leaks, or blown circuits. Knowing where projects typically trip up helps you plan a smooth installation.

Common Mistakes to Avoid
- Treating hardwired units as simple plug-ins: Many modern cooktops, wall ovens, and high-draw appliances require direct, hardwired electrical connections on dedicated circuits. Avoid assuming your old junction box matches current manufacturer requirements without checking the cut sheet.
- Trapping shutoff valves behind appliances: Placing water or gas shutoffs in the wrong spot can prevent your stove or refrigerator from pushing flush against the wall. Position shutoff valves within accessible lower cabinet bases or approved wall recesses so they remain easy to reach in an emergency.
- Reusing degraded supply lines or venting ducts: Hooking up a new dishwasher with old flexible hoses or connecting a range hood to undersized, corrugated foil ducts invites leaks and airflow restrictions. Always use manufacturer-specified rigid or semi-rigid materials and fresh fittings.
- Skipping operational leak and airflow tests: Never slide appliances permanently into place before running complete test cycles. Checking for water leaks under full pressure, verifying proper electrical grounding, and confirming exterior vent dampers open freely prevents damage to new cabinets and flooring.

When Professional Guidance Helps
